info.title: Vortex Chess API
info.description: Authentication (milestone 1) plus private rooms, invitations, notifications and Socket.IO realtime (milestone 2). Bearer access JWT in frontend memory; rotating HttpOnly refresh cookie for /auth/refresh only. All responses use Cache-Control: no-store. Realtime events are documented in docs/Rooms_Invitations_Notifications_Milestone.md (Socket.IO path /api/socket.io). No email address of another account ever appears in these payloads. Email ownership is not verified; invitations bind to account ids, and email is only a lookup key and the offline delivery address. Participant-only finished-game history and isolated, temporary manual analysis are implemented; See docs/History_Replay_Analysis_Milestone.md. Player-versus-engine games are implemented: the backend alone calls the engine service over HTTP/JSON; engine moves use the same authoritative pipeline (docs/Engine_Gameplay_Milestone.md). Engine evaluation, hints and automated review remain unavailable. Rated random human matchmaking, elo-v1 settlement and paginated competition-rank leaderboards are implemented (docs/Rated_Matchmaking_Elo_Leaderboards.md). Historical, friend and engine games remain casual. Friends/social management is implemented with durable requests, unique friendships, directional blocks, private friend presence, existing casual invitations and block-aware random pairing. See docs/Friends_Social_Management.md.

post.summary: Validate an untimed temporary variation from a recorded position
post.description: Participants only; game must be finished. Replays initialFen and recorded prefix up to basePly, checks SAN/FEN integrity, then applies the UCI path in an isolated chess.js instance. Returns every validated SAN/FEN plus final turn, check and legal destinations for the side to move. No writes, session table, clock changes, live events or engine calls. Earlier positions remain explorable after mate/resignation/timeout. FEN input and unknown fields are rejected. Do not automatically retry illegal moves.

404.description: game_not_found; missing game or not a participant

422.description: illegal_analysis_move; includes the failing 1-based variation index

503.description: game_integrity_error; recorded prefix cannot be reconstructed

get.description: Whether an engine game can start now, from the engine service health (cached 5 s). Health is not a reservation or proof of search capacity.

401.description: Missing, expired or revoked access token

post.description: Starts a game against the engine service with the room setup contract (a supported preset and a colour preference). Readiness (fresh health check) and the admission limit (ENGINE_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES, one active engine game per account) are checked before the clock starts; the game is created in one transaction. If the engine plays White its opening search starts after the commit. Moves and resignation then use the ordinary game endpoints and the `game:<id>` channel; draw offers are refused with 409 draw_offers_unavailable.

409.description: engine_game_active: the account already has an active engine game; the body adds `gameId`.

503.description: engine_unavailable (retryable: the service is unreachable or not ready), engine_capacity_reached (retryable: admission limit), engine_not_configured

post.summary: Join rated or casual random human matchmaking
post.description: Defaults to casual for old clients. Only backend-mapped bullet/blitz/rapid presets support rated mode. Both current rating windows must allow the pair. Existing search is idempotent; a different mode or clock conflicts. Server derives identity, pool and rating. No client ratings, result or deltas are accepted.

outcome.description: `aborted`: an engine game ended because the engine service failed after bounded recovery; no winner and no draw are recorded.

players.description: Seats by colour. `kind: "engine"` is the engine service: id is the literal "engine" (never an account id), username is the name it reported at game creation.

EngineTurn.description: The engine's search for the current turn. Not game state: it never changes the revision, and it describes the game only while `revision` equals the game's revision.

phase.description: queued: waiting for a search slot; thinking: request in flight; retrying: a transient service failure is being retried.

since.description: Server time (epoch ms) this phase began.

id.description: Account id (UUID), or "engine" for the engine seat.

online.description: Players: at least one connection. Always true for the engine.

EngineStatus.description: Engine readiness for display, cached for up to 5 s. It reserves nothing.

engine.description: Name reported by the engine service.

HistoryOpponent.description: The other seat. For engine games: id "engine" (never an account id), the name the engine service reported, kind "engine".
